The Cepheus Flare is in reality several individually Gaia-resolved dark clouds (L1148, L1158, L1177, L1217, L1219, L1235, L1251, L1228) spanning 330-368 pc (Dzib et al. 2021, MNRAS, 505, 5164, 'The Gaia view of the Cepheus flare', arXiv:2105.10039); the complex also spans ~90x60 pc in the plane of the sky per that paper (visual.size_pc uses the larger axis). This record collapses that structure to one MVP centroid using the Zucker et al. 2019 'Cepheus Near' value, which falls within the Dzib range.

objects.name: Cepheus OB2

source.reference: Szilagyi, M., Kun, M., Abraham, P. & Marton, G. (2023), "The Gaia view of the Cepheus OB2 association", MNRAS, 520(1), 1390-1410 (arXiv:2301.02346). Gaia DR3 clustering resolves the association into 13 subgroups spanning heliocentric distances of 829-944 pc along the line of sight, centred at Galactic (l,b) = (102.1 deg, +4.6 deg); the classical literature value (Contreras et al. 2002, ApJ, 572, 926) is ~900 pc. distance_pc/error_pc here are the midpoint/half-range of the quoted Gaia DR3 829-944 pc subgroup spread, not a formal single-value parallax uncertainty - no single-number mean distance + error is given in the source for the association as a whole.

objects.notes: Position is the SIMBAD 'Ass Cep OB 2' centroid (ra=327.75, dec=60.0 deg), independently verified to correspond to Galactic (l,b) = (102.11, 4.64) deg, matching Szilagyi et al. (2023)'s quoted central coordinates for the association.

objects.name: Cepheus OB3

source.reference: Nagy, Zs., Abraham, P., Kospal, A. et al. (2022), "Photometric and spectroscopic study of the burst-like brightening of two Gaia-alerted young stellar objects", MNRAS, 516, 2. Distance to Cep OB3 of 816 +/- 53 pc obtained from a Gaussian fit to Gaia EDR3 parallax-based distances (Bailer-Jones et al. 2021) of 235 quality-filtered (RUWE < 1.4, parallax significant > 5 sigma) association members drawn from Jordi et al. (1996) and Getman et al. (2009).

objects.notes: Position is the SIMBAD 'NAME III CEP ASSOC' centroid.

objects.name: Cepheus OB4

source.reference: Wiesneth, B., Muzic, K. & Almendros-Abad, V. (2025), "Internal dynamics and structure of Cepheus OB4: The asymmetric expansion of Berkeley 59", A&A, 703, A193 (arXiv:2509.19175). Gaia DR3 astrometry gives a distance of 1009 +/- 12 pc to Berkeley 59, the dominant central massive-star cluster of the Cep OB4 association / H II bubble.

objects.notes: Position and distance are for Berkeley 59 (SIMBAD 'Cl Berkeley 59'), the dominant central cluster of Cep OB4 - its SIMBAD position (ra=0.57, dec=67.441) matches the wider association's own SIMBAD centroid ('Ass Cep OB 4', ra=0.50, dec=67.70) to within 0.3 deg. Earlier literature (Kun, Kiss & Balog 2008, Handbook of Star Forming Regions Vol. I, arXiv:0809.4761) placed the Cep OB2/OB3/OB4 group collectively at a coarser 600-900 pc range; the Gaia DR3 Berkeley 59 value is adopted here as the more precise, modern figure.

objects.name: Chamaeleon Molecular Cloud

source.reference: Position: SIMBAD, "NAME Chamaeleon I" / "NAME Cha 1" (identification only; RA/Dec used here are astropy-transformed coordinates of the nearest matching Zucker+2020 sightline, l=297.5 deg, b=-15.3 deg, Table A.1 row "Chamaeleon", Star Formation Handbook Southern volume p.169). Distance: Zucker, C., Speagle, J. S., Schlafly, E. F., Green, G. M., Finkbeiner, D. P., Goodman, A. A., & Alves, J. (2020), "A compendium of distances to molecular clouds in the Star Formation Handbook", Astronomy & Astrophysics, 633, A51 (arXiv:2001.00591). Distance is the reported median cloud distance (Table A.1) for the tabulated Star Formation Handbook sightline nearest this object's SIMBAD-catalogued named position (see notes for the exact sightline and l/b used); RA/Dec stored here are transformed from that sightline's published Galactic (l, b) via astropy.coordinates (no new position measurement is made - this is a coordinate-representation conversion of the published value, consistent with spec Idea.md §6's astropy-only transform requirement). distance.error_pc is sqrt(mean(statistical +/-)^2 + systematic^2), combined in quadrature as the paper itself recommends (Table A.1, note 4).
source.catalog: Zucker et al. 2020 (SF Handbook compendium, Table A.1)

objects.notes: SIMBAD centroid for Chamaeleon I specifically (ra=166.7, dec=-77.3, coo_bibcode 2000PASA...17...92O) used only to identify the named region; final position is the Zucker+2020 sightline closest to that centroid (l,b offset ~0.5 deg), RA/Dec=168.6420, -77.1386. Table A.1 statistical uncertainty +15/-11 pc, systematic ~7% for this NSC-footprint cloud (14 pc); combined in quadrature -> 19.1 pc. Broadly consistent with other Cha I distance determinations (~191 pc, e.g. Voirin et al. 2018, A&A, 610, A54; Zucker's own sightline set used here samples a slightly different part of the Chamaeleon complex, hence the modest offset).

objects.name: Local Bubble

source.reference: Alves, M.I.R., Boulanger, F., Ferriere, K. & Montier, L. (2018), "The Local Bubble: a magnetic veil to our Galaxy", A&A, 611, L5 (doi:10.1051/0004-6361/201832637). Center position reused from Story #62's models/local_bubble.yaml ellipsoid-model center_pc = (x=10.2, y=33.6, z=0.0) pc, itself Alves et al. (2018) Table 1's fitted off-centred-spheroid offset (Sun at 0.58 of the semi-minor axis from the ellipsoid centre, along l=73 deg, b~0 deg) scaled by the paper's approximate a_pc=60 pc physical anchor (Sec. 1, citing Puspitarini et al. 2014, A&A, 566, A13).

objects.notes: This is a single-point/centroid catalog-object representation of the Local Bubble (spec Idea.md §9 seed list, §15 MVP 'center + approximate radius' allowance), distinct from the separate, more detailed ellipsoid geometry in Story #62's models/local_bubble.yaml (which this entry deliberately does not duplicate or modify). No formal uncertainty is available for the centroid position itself in the source (Alves et al. 2018 fit shape/orientation, not an absolute distance, with error bars only on the dimensionless shape parameters - see models/local_bubble.yaml for those); the 60 pc anchor behind this position, and visual.size_pc here (approximating the semi-minor axis as a representative radius), are both order-of-magnitude, not precision-fit, figures. Position/distance were reverse-derived from center_pc via astropy Galactic->ICRS and round-trip verified to reproduce x=10.2, y=33.6, z=0.0 pc through this project's own coordinates.derive_galactic_coordinates().

objects.name: Lupus Molecular Cloud

source.reference: Position: SIMBAD, "Lupus 1" (identification only; RA/Dec used here are astropy-transformed coordinates of the nearest matching Zucker+2020 sightline, l=339.0 deg, b=16.3 deg, Table A.1 row "Lupus", Star Formation Handbook Southern volume p.295). Distance: Zucker, C., Speagle, J. S., Schlafly, E. F., Green, G. M., Finkbeiner, D. P., Goodman, A. A., & Alves, J. (2020), "A compendium of distances to molecular clouds in the Star Formation Handbook", Astronomy & Astrophysics, 633, A51 (arXiv:2001.00591). Distance is the reported median cloud distance (Table A.1) for the tabulated Star Formation Handbook sightline nearest this object's SIMBAD-catalogued named position (see notes for the exact sightline and l/b used); RA/Dec stored here are transformed from that sightline's published Galactic (l, b) via astropy.coordinates (no new position measurement is made - this is a coordinate-representation conversion of the published value, consistent with spec Idea.md §6's astropy-only transform requirement). distance.error_pc is sqrt(mean(statistical +/-)^2 + systematic^2), combined in quadrature as the paper itself recommends (Table A.1, note 4).
source.catalog: Zucker et al. 2020 (SF Handbook compendium, Table A.1)

objects.notes: SIMBAD centroid for the Lupus 1 sub-cloud (ra=235.76, dec=-34.15) used only to identify the named region; final position is the Zucker+2020 sightline closest to that centroid (l,b offset ~0.2 deg), RA/Dec=235.9739, -34.2287. Table A.1 statistical uncertainty +13/-11 pc, systematic ~7% for this NSC-footprint cloud (10 pc, per the paper's Table A.1 footnote 4); combined in quadrature -> 15.6 pc. The Lupus region as a whole (Lupus I-IV) spans several sub-clouds at somewhat different distances (~150-200 pc); this record represents the Lupus 1 sightline as a single representative centroid for the MVP (spec §15).

objects.name: Scorpius-Centaurus Association

source.reference: de Zeeuw, P. T., Hoogerwerf, R., de Bruijne, J. H. J., Brown, A. G. A., Blaauw, A. 1999, AJ, 117, 354, 'A HIPPARCOS Census of the Nearby OB Associations' - mean subgroup distances: Upper Scorpius (US) 145 pc, Upper Centaurus-Lupus (UCL) 140 pc, Lower Centaurus-Crux (LCC) 118 pc. Still the standard subgroup-distance reference used by Gaia-era Sco-Cen studies (e.g. Damiani, F., et al. 2019, A&A, 623, A112, arXiv:1807.11884, which restricts its Gaia DR2 census to <200 pc and finds ~90% of known massive members within 100-170 pc, consistent with these subgroup values rather than superseding them with one number).
source.catalog: Hipparcos (de Zeeuw et al. 1999); consistent with Gaia DR2 (Damiani et al. 2019)

objects.notes: Sco-Cen is the nearest OB association to the Sun but comprises 3 kinematically/spatially distinct subgroups (Upper Sco, Upper Cen-Lup, Lower Cen-Crux) spanning tens of pc in depth - the current schema has no sub-group representation, so this is deliberately simplified to a single MVP centroid, per issue #59 guidance. distance_pc is the unweighted mean of the 3 published subgroup distances (134.3 pc); distance.error_pc is the population standard deviation across those 3 subgroups (11.7 pc) - this is a depth-spread proxy, NOT a formal parallax/fit uncertainty, and should not be conflated with one. Position (ra/dec) is taken from the SIMBAD entry 'NAME Upper Sco-Cen' (otype As*), the closest single-point designation SIMBAD offers for the complex as a whole. A future story could add the 3 subgroups as separate records with `group.primary` set to this association's id.

objects.name: Vela Supernova Remnant

source.reference: Dodson, R., Legge, D., Reynolds, J.E. & McCulloch, P.M. (2003), "The Vela Pulsar's Proper Motion and Parallax Derived from VLBI Observations", ApJ, 596, 1137 (arXiv:astro-ph/0302374). VLBI parallax of the embedded pulsar PSR B0833-45 = 3.4 +/- 0.2 mas, equivalent to a distance of 293 (+19/-17) pc; adopted here as the remnant's distance per standard convention that the Vela SNR shares the distance of its associated pulsar.

objects.notes: Coordinates are those of the embedded pulsar PSR B0833-45 (SIMBAD 'NAME Vela Pulsar'), ~0.4 deg from the SIMBAD-catalogued extended-remnant centroid ('NAME Vela', SNR G263.9-03.3; ra=128.5, dec=-45.833) - within the remnant's ~4 deg angular radius and negligible (~2 pc) at this distance. error_pc uses the larger (+19 pc) of the source's asymmetric +19/-17 pc uncertainty, since this schema's error_pc is a single symmetric value. visual.size_pc ~= 40 pc is an approximate physical diameter derived from the remnant's commonly quoted ~8 deg angular diameter (ROSAT X-ray survey era literature, e.g. Aschenbach 1998 and successors) at the adopted VLBI distance - an order-of-magnitude figure, not a formally fitted size.

objects.name: Corona Australis Molecular Cloud

source.reference: Position: SIMBAD, "NAME Corona Australis Cloud" (identification only; otype MoC, ra=285.4625, dec=-36.9817 - used solely to identify the region and pick the nearest tabulated sightline below; RA/Dec stored here are the VizieR-computed ICRS coordinates, _RA.icrs/_DE.icrs, of that nearest sightline itself, l=359.5 deg, b=-17.8 deg). Distance: Zucker, C., Speagle, J. S., Schlafly, E. F., Green, G. M., Finkbeiner, D. P., Goodman, A. A., & Alves, J. (2020), "A compendium of distances to molecular clouds in the Star Formation Handbook", Astronomy & Astrophysics, 633, A51 (arXiv:2001.00591). Live-queried the real, machine-readable VizieR table J/A+A/633/A51/handbook (astroquery.vizier, all columns, not any scraped/summarized prose version of the paper) for the 'Corona_Australis'-named sightline group (3 rows, 147-165 pc) and took the row nearest the SIMBAD identification position by angular separation (0.386 deg): d50=147 pc, d16=142 pc, d84=152 pc. distance.error_pc = sqrt(mean(|d50-d16|,|d84-d50|)^2 + systematic^2) = sqrt(5.0^2 + 10.29^2) = 11.44 pc, using the paper's own explicitly-named ~7% systematic for 'the southern clouds Lupus, Chamaeleon, and Corona Australis' (ReadMe), not the general ~5%.
source.catalog: Zucker et al. 2020 (SF Handbook compendium, VizieR J/A+A/633/A51/handbook)

objects.notes: Story #318 new-record gap-fill (data/raw/gap_fills/README.md convention, adapted for molecular clouds): one of the catalog's original 8 molecular_cloud records (spec Idea.md §9's minimum seed list) never expanded beyond it; this is one of the issue's own strong, well-under-800pc candidates - one of the nearest star-forming regions, parent cloud of the Coronet Cluster. visual.size_pc is a DIAMETER (this catalog's established molecular_cloud convention, confirmed twice by Story #314's independent validator passes) derived from SIMBAD's own galdim_majaxis=600.0 arcmin for 'NAME Corona Australis Cloud' (bibcode 2018MNRAS.474.4672L) via this record's own distance_pc, the same data_sources.simbad_size.resolve_angular_diameter/diameter_pc_from_angular_size pair Story #314 established, queried live for this new record rather than backfilled after the fact.

objects.name: Coalsack Nebula

source.reference: Position: SIMBAD, "NAME Coalsack Nebula" (identification only; otype DNe, aliases NAME Coalsack/NAME Southern Coalsack/NAME COAL SACK, ra=187.829, dec=-63.743 - used solely to identify the region and pick the nearest tabulated sightline below; RA/Dec stored here are the VizieR-computed ICRS coordinates, _RA.icrs/_DE.icrs, of that nearest sightline itself, l=301.4 deg, b=-2.6 deg). Live-queried the real, machine-readable VizieR table J/A+A/633/A51/handbook for the 'Coalsack'-named sightline group (6 rows, 182-193 pc, all in close agreement) and took the row nearest the SIMBAD identification position by angular separation (1.78 deg - looser than this Story's other 3 new records since the Coalsack's own real angular extent is large, ~7x5 deg on the sky, but still the closest tabulated sightline and within the same named group): d50=182 pc, d16=176 pc, d84=187 pc. distance.error_pc = sqrt(mean(|d50-d16|,|d84-d50|)^2 + systematic^2) = sqrt(5.5^2 + 9.1^2) = 10.63 pc, using the paper's general ~5% systematic for clouds <1.5kpc (the Coalsack is not one of the three southern clouds the paper singles out for the higher ~7% figure).

objects.notes: Story #318 new-record gap-fill (data/raw/gap_fills/README.md convention, adapted for molecular clouds): the famous naked-eye dark nebula next to the Southern Cross, one of the issue's own strong, well-under-800pc candidates. visual.size_pc is an honest failure, left null: every SIMBAD alias of this object ('NAME Coalsack Nebula', 'NAME Coalsack', 'NAME Southern Coalsack', 'NAME COAL SACK') was queried live against data_sources.simbad_size.resolve_angular_diameter and none carries a galdim_majaxis on file for the named object as a whole (a targeted SIMBAD TAP search for extended objects with galdim data within 5 deg of this position turned up only much smaller individual sub-clumps/globules, not a size for the Coalsack itself) - the same 'resolved identifier, no angular-size measurement' honest-failure shape Story #314 hit for M8/the Lagoon Nebula. objects.notes: Story #318 new-record gap-fill (data/raw/gap_fills/README.md convention, adapted for molecular clouds): the actively star-forming core of the Serpens cloud, resolving the issue's own 'Serpens/Aquila Rift complex' weaker/optional candidate. The real Zucker+2020 table shows 'Serpens'/'Serpens_Main' and 'Aquila_Rift' are genuinely DISTINCT sightline groups at different median distances (Aquila_Rift's own 5 tabulated sightlines run 163-280 pc, well short of Serpens'/Serpens_Main's ~425-556 pc) - not one combined complex, contrary to the issue's own '260-440pc per inconsistent secondary sources' framing. Aquila Rift was investigated as a possible separate record but NOT added: SIMBAD's own single-point identification for it ('NAME Aql Rift', ra=278.0, dec=-1.0) sits >9 deg from every one of the Zucker table's own 'Aquila_Rift'-named rows (nearest same-named row 9.586 deg away), while its SIMBAD galdim_majaxis (1530 arcmin, ~25.5 deg) confirms it is an enormous extended superposition/extinction feature spanning much of the sky, not a single coherent cloud - a poor fit for this catalog's single-point/single-distance object model, and not force-fit here (honest exclusion, not a fabricated match). This Serpens Molecular Cloud record stands alone as the cleanly resolvable representative of the issue's combined candidate. visual.size_pc is an honest failure, left null: 'NAME Serpens Main Cloud' and several tried aliases (Serpens, Serpens Cloud Core, Serpens dark cloud, Serpens Nebula, Serpens South, GF 9, W 40, Serpens molecular cloud core, MWSC 2790) were queried live against data_sources.simbad_size.resolve_angular_diameter; only 'W 40' and 'GF 9' returned a galdim value, but both are small, specific, physically distinct sub-features (an embedded HII region and an unrelated dark cloud, respectively, each at their own different sightline distance) rather than a size for Serpens Main Cloud itself, so neither is used. Never fabricated/approximated.

source.notes: Center XYZ derived from the paper's reported (distance=104pc, l=180.4deg, b=0) via this repo's Galactic Cartesian convention (spec §6); orientation_deg is the paper's ascending-node longitude l_Omega=296.1deg. All other fields are the paper's fitted values verbatim (see comments above).

source.reference: Konietzka, R., Goodman, A. A., Zucker, C., Burkert, A., Alves, J., Foley, M., Swiggum, C., Koller, M. & Miret-Roig, N. (2024), "The Radcliffe Wave is oscillating", Nature, 626, 63-68
source.notes: arXiv:2402.12596. Points are the paper's own published best-fit model spine (file 'Radcliffe_Wave_best_fit_model_Konietzka2024.tab', CC0-licensed), i.e. the fitted/interpolated curve, not raw individual cloud or cluster measurements - see 'curve_type' and this module's docstring. Raw file kept unmodified at data/raw/Radcliffe_Wave_best_fit_model_Konietzka2024.tab (spec §13). s_pc is this repo's own derived cumulative 3D arclength along the file's point ordering (not a column in the source file). The source file's x, y, z columns are stated by the paper (Methods, 'Full Spatial and Kinematic Model') to be Heliocentric Galactic Cartesian coordinates, matching spec §6's convention; the source file's fourth column, vz (line-of-sight velocity), is not part of this Story's spatial schema and is not carried into models/radcliffe_wave.csv.

radcliffe_wave.notes: This is the interpolated/fitted Radcliffe Wave curve (Konietzka et al. 2024's published best-fit spine), not observed cloud positions. It does not replace the individual astronomical objects (e.g. Taurus, Perseus, Orion) that make up the Wave - those are separate catalog entries (spec §7) tracked elsewhere.

source.reference: Alves, M.I.R., Boulanger, F., Ferriere, K. & Montier, L. (2018), "The Local Bubble: a magnetic veil to our Galaxy", Astronomy & Astrophysics, 611, L5. Table 1 gives the fitted shape (aspect ratio c_ell/a_ell = 2.7 +/- 0.6), orientation (Euler angles, and the long axis pointing towards l=216 deg, b=60 deg), and the Sun's offset as a fraction of the semi-minor axis (0.58, along l=73 deg, b~0 deg) - all obtained by fitting an off-centred prolate-spheroid shell model to Planck 353 GHz dust polarization observations of the Galactic polar caps.
source.secondary_reference: IMPORTANT CAVEAT on absolute scale: dust polarization data alone carry no distance information, so Alves et al. (2018) fit their spheroid in normalized units with the semi-minor axis fixed to 1 (aell = bell = 1, set - see their Table 1 and Sec. 3). The `semi_axes_pc` and `center_pc` values in this file were produced by multiplying those dimensionless, precisely-fitted shape/orientation /offset-fraction numbers by an approximate physical scale anchor of a_pc = 60 pc, taken from the paper's own Sec. 1 description of the Local Bubble "extending out to ~60 pc towards the Galactic centre ... (Puspitarini et al. 2014)" - itself citing Puspitarini, R., Lallement, R., Vergely, J.-L. & Snowden, S.L. (2014), Astronomy & Astrophysics, 566, A13. This 60 pc anchor is an approximate, order-of-magnitude figure, not a quantity fitted jointly with the shape/orientation parameters above - treat `semi_axes_pc` and `center_pc` as illustrative-scale, not precision-fit, values.

local_bubble.notes: MVP simplified volume per spec Idea.md §18. A coarse off-centred spheroid approximation of the Local Bubble shell, intended to be replaced by a more realistic 3D reconstruction later without renderer changes (see module docstring in local_bubble.py for the intended extension path).
